correctness.rationale: For the exact facets v+Q modulo 23, the embedded standard-library checker enumerates all 42,297 nonempty faces; verifies 19,184 elementary simplicial collapses to 3,929 faces; constructs and checks a complete acyclic Hasse matching with critical cells (1 in degree zero, 212 in degree three, 4 in degree four); and calculates the integral 212-by-4 Morse boundary. An exact column relation gives rank at most 3; a displayed 3-by-3 minor of determinant -1 gives rank at least 3 and primitive image, hence Smith invariants (1,1,1,0). By Hurewicz for the two-connected three-skeleton and classification of four-cell attachments, the resulting CW complex is a wedge of 209 three-spheres and one four-sphere. All computations replayed from the actual standalone checker; finite enumeration is exhaustive for the precisely stated 23-vertex complex.

value.rationale: The 23-vertex quadratic-residue tournament is a canonical doubly regular tournament and its out-neighborhood blocks form the classical symmetric Paley 2-(23,11,5) design. The cited 2021 paper explicitly asks which homotopy types arise as tournament neighborhood complexes. The mixed-dimensional wedge is an exact homotopy answer to that motivated problem, with integral third and fourth homology and primitive attachments that are not specified by design parameters, ordinary dimension bounds or ranks over a finite field. The fact is intrinsic to a natural finite geometry, not an arbitrary slice.
